name: Length Matching Budget
blurb: maximum length mismatch for a bus speed, in ps and mm
intro: Turns a bit rate into the length mismatch routing may use: a share of the unit interval (UI = 1/bit rate), divided by the trace's propagation delay from εr (stripline) or Hammerstad-Jensen εeff (microstrip).

inputs.label: Bit rate per lane
inputs.help: 5G = 5 Gb/s. For DDR give the transfer rate, e.g. 3200M.

inputs.label: What is being matched
options: P to N inside one pair (5 % UI)
Lane to lane / data to strobe (10 % UI)
Slow parallel bus to clock (15 % UI)

inputs.label: Custom share of UI
inputs.help: Only used when 'Custom share of UI' is picked.

inputs.label: Microstrip width / height
inputs.help: Trace width over the height to the plane; about 2 for 50 Ω on FR-4. Ignored for stripline.

examples.title: DDR4-3200 byte lane on inner layers
PCIe Gen3 pair on the top layer

usage: Give the bit rate per lane in bit/s (engineering notation: 5G, 3200M), what is being matched (intra, lanes, bus or custom with share in %), the layer (stripline or microstrip), εr and, for microstrip, the width/height ratio. It returns the UI, the skew budget in ps, the maximum length mismatch in mm and mil, and the propagation delay in ps/mm, plus tables for other shares and rates. Use it to set a length-tuning tolerance when the interface's own guide gives none.
sources: Unit interval and skew budget: rule of thumb from high-speed layout guides (e.g. TI SPRAAR7 High-Speed Interface Layout Guidelines)
Microstrip effective permittivity: Hammerstad & Jensen, 'Accurate models for microstrip computer-aided design', IEEE MTT-S 1980
Propagation delay t = sqrt(εeff)/c: Johnson & Graham, High-Speed Digital Design, ch. 4
